    AI Overview
    The Masters uses a sudden-death playoff format if golfers are tied after 72 holes. Players immediately play the 18th hole, and if still tied, proceed to the 10th hole, alternating between the two until a winner is decided. This format, adopted in 1976, has been used 12 times since 1979. 
    This video explains the sudden-death playoff format at the Masters:
    58s
    HD SHORTS
    YouTube• Apr 13, 2025
    • Hole Rotation: 18th hole
      →right arrow
       10th hole
      →right arrow
       18th hole....
    • Sudden-Death Rule: The first player to win a hole outright (i.e., achieves a better score than the opponent on that specific hole) is declared the champion.
    • History: The last playoff occurred in 2025, when Rory McIlroy defeated Justin Rose.
    • Past Formats:
      Previously, the Masters used an 18-hole playoff on Monday, and before that, a 36-hole playoff.
       
    No sudden-death playoff in Masters history has ever gone beyond two holes.

    What is the Masters playoff format?
    Playoffs begin on No. 18. If that hole doesn't produce a winner, the playoff moves to No. 10, and the two-hole rotation repeats until a winner emerges. The format makes sound logistical sense, as the 18th and 10th run mostly parallel to each other, making it easier on both spectators and competitors.7 hours ago

    What happens if the Masters ends in tie?
    Well, we have the answer. Much like the PGA Tour if two or more players are tied after the 72nd hole the golfers involved will head to a sudden-death playoff. This means that the first player to win a hole will be crowned champion and be putting on the Green Jacket that evening.Apr 13, 2025
